questions.question: Why is prompt-only 'return JSON' not enough for production?
options: JSON is too verbose a format, so it wastes context tokens compared to a more compact serialization like YAML
Native structured-output APIs already guarantee 100% valid JSON on every provider, so plain prompting is a redundant, wasted step
Frontier models comply most of the time but not always; the small fraction of malformed outputs still breaks downstream parsers
Prompting is fundamentally unable to describe a schema at all, so the model has no idea what fields are expected
questions.explanation: Prompt-only structure works ~80% of the time on frontier models; production needs harder guarantees.

questions.question: What does constrained decoding modify at each generation step?
options: The logit vector, masking tokens that would invalidate the target grammar so only valid continuations can be sampled
The KV cache, evicting entries for any token that does not match the target schema's expected structure
The tokenizer's vocabulary, temporarily removing invalid subword tokens before the next forward pass
The training loss, penalizing the model's gradient whenever it emits a token that falls outside the target grammar entirely
questions.explanation: A logit processor sets invalid tokens to -inf so the softmax cannot sample them.

questions.question: Why might constrained decoding be faster than free generation?
options: It swaps in a smaller distilled model automatically whenever a schema-constrained request is detected
Forced scaffold tokens (e.g. '{"name": "') can be emitted directly without sampling, and the valid-token search space shrinks
It avoids running softmax entirely by short-circuiting straight from logits to the final output tokens
It skips backpropagation entirely, since the logit processor supposedly already knows what the correct final answer will be
questions.explanation: Determined tokens skip sampling and reduced valid-token sets shrink the decode cost.

questions.question: Which schema design choice prevents premature commitment by the model?
options: Putting the 'answer' field first, so the model states its conclusion before it has generated any of the supporting reasoning text
Using shorter field key names, since shorter keys reduce the number of tokens the model has to commit to
Using snake_case field names instead of camelCase, since the tokenizer handles underscores more predictably
Placing reasoning fields before the answer/decision field, so the model works through the logic before committing to an answer
questions.explanation: Field order is logic: putting reasoning first lets the model think before locking in an answer.

questions.question: What is the limitation of FSM-based constrained decoding tools like Outlines?
options: Recursive schemas have to be flattened; truly recursive structures need CFG-based engines such as XGrammar
They are not deterministic, so the same schema and prompt can still produce different structures across runs
They lock you to OpenAI's API, since finite-state machines only compile against OpenAI's proprietary schema format
They only support enum-typed fields, so any schema with strings or numbers falls back to free-form generation
questions.explanation: FSMs cannot represent unbounded recursion; CFG engines handle it.

questions.question: Why is Instructor described as not modifying logits?
options: It applies live gradient updates during inference to nudge the model's weights toward producing valid outputs
Instructor formats the schema into the prompt and parses/retries the output; logit masking happens server-side or not at all
Anthropic's terms of service require third-party libraries to avoid touching raw logits directly
It only edits the prompt text, without ever validating or retrying against the returned response
questions.explanation: Instructor uses provider-side structured output plus client-side validation and retries, not logit masking.

questions.question: What problem can a strict regex like date='YYYY-MM-DD' introduce?
options: It requires switching from an FSM engine to a full CFG engine just to represent a single strict date field
It breaks JSON parsing entirely, since regex-constrained fields cannot be embedded inside a JSON object
Regex matching is inherently too slow to run at every generation step during decoding
It removes any escape hatch for unknown values, so the model fabricates a date instead of returning null/sentinel
questions.explanation: Over-strict grammars force the model to invent values; always allow null/sentinel for unknowns.

questions.question: When should you reach for vLLM guided decoding vs a vendor structured-output API?
options: Always prefer the vendor API, since it is guaranteed to outperform any self-hosted decoding setup
Only for very small schemas, since vLLM's guided decoding cannot handle nested or recursive structures
Self-hosted inference where you control the model and want logit-level guarantees without relying on retries
Only when the tokenizer uses byte-level BPE, since other tokenization schemes are incompatible with guided decoding
questions.explanation: vLLM guided decoding fits self-hosted serving with logit-level constraints; vendor APIs lock you to their stack.
